about.title: Personal Injury Help in Milpitas, California
about.longDescription: Milpitas sits where three major routes meet: I-880 along the west side, I-680 to the east, and Route 237 cutting across toward the bay. Those same corridors also carry the highest collision counts in the city's public records. In 2025, the most recent final year on file, Milpitas logged 243 injury collisions, with 318 people hurt and 4 traffic deaths. Records show reported crashes tend to peak on Thursdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. Behind each of those figures is a real person dealing with pain, missed shifts, and a phone that will not stop ringing with adjusters. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury claims in Milpitas and throughout Santa Clara County. We work on contingency, which means you pay no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether you were hurt on the freeway, on a bike, or at a job site, a short conversation can help you understand your options before California's filing deadlines run out. Reaching out costs nothing and commits you to nothing.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Milpitas Claim

items.title: Two Years Is Shorter Than It Sounds
items.desc: California gives most injury victims two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit, but claims against a city, county, or state agency can require notice in as little as six months. Getting in touch early keeps those doors open.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partly responsible reduces your recovery by your share of blame but never wipes it out. Even a driver found mostly at fault can still pursue compensation.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no statutory limit on non-economic damages like pain, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life. We can help document those losses properly.

items.title: Contingency Fees Only
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Where do crashes in Milpitas tend to happen?
items.answer: Public collision records show the highest counts along I-880, I-680, and Route 237, the three major routes that pass through the city. Reported crashes also peak on Thursdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are neutral counts from public data, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Milpitas?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. If a government entity such as a city or transit agency may be responsible, you may need to submit a formal claim within six months. Because the rules vary, it helps to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We are a personal injury law practice that handles claims directly in Milpitas and Santa Clara County. We do not give legal advice beyond the scope of your case, and we represent you, not multiple clients simultaneously through a referral service.

items.question: What will it cost me to hire your firm?
items.answer: Nothing up front. We work on contingency, meaning we are paid only if there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Does it matter that I may have contributed to the crash?
items.answer: It can affect the amount you recover, but it does not disqualify you. California follows pure comparative fault, so your compensation is reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated. We can review the facts and explain how fault might be assigned in your situation.
